chunks: My father, may Allah grant him mercy, said: We were told by Muhammad ibn Yahya al-‘Attar, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Yazid, from al-Husayn ibn A’yan, the brother of Malik ibn A’yan, that he said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the saying of one man to another: “May Allah reward you with goodness”, what does he mean by it?

Then Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: Indeed, Goodness is a river in Paradise whose emergence is from the Kawthar, and the emergence of Kawthar is from the Leg of the Throne, upon which are the ranks of the Successors and their Shi’a. On the two sides of that river are sprouting maids; whenever one is pulled off, another sprouts with the name of that river, and that is the saying of Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He, in His Book: “In them are beautiful goods”.

So, when one man says to his companion: “May Allah reward you with goodness”, he only means by it those ranks which Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He, has prepared for His chosen and selected from among His creation.

key_terms.الْخَيْر: Goodness (specifically referring to the spiritual ranks of the Imams)
key_terms.الْكَوْثَر: The River of Abundance in Paradise

ai.seo_question: What is the theological meaning behind saying 'Jazak Allah Khair' in Shia tradition?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Mani al-Akhbar*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) elucidates that the phrase 'Jazak Allahu khairan' invokes the specific spiritual stations of the Imams and their followers, which are situated along the River of Goodness (an-Nahr) in Paradise. This river originates from the Kawthar, flowing from the Leg of the Throne, thereby linking the supplication directly to the cosmic hierarchy of the Ahl al-Bayt. The explanation connects the linguistic act of gratitude to the tangible, eternal rewards prepared for the divine elect, emphasizing the intercessory and hierarchical nature of Shia eschatology.
